sources.citation: I. G. Gjerde and L. R. Scott, Verification and validation of cylinder drag: Pressure and stress approximations on curved boundaries, Advances in Computational Science and Engineering 2(3), 295-319 (2024), DOI 10.3934/acse.2024015
facts_used: strong Scott-Vogelius on polygonal curved boundary exhibits roughly h^(1/2) H1 error in the manufactured test
Nitsche table uses k=4, N_Gamma=32 N_Omega, mu=100, with observed rates 2.059, 1.116, 1.834
published drag computations also use mu=1e6
published article says relaxing boundary conditions with Nitsche restores high-order approximation

sources.citation: I. G. Gjerde and L. R. Scott, arXiv:2306.12362v1 (2023)
facts_used: manufactured divergence-free solution is curl(log r - r^2/2) with constant pressure
Scott-Vogelius velocity degree k=4 in the reported experiment
preprint notation defines V_h with zero trace on Gamma_h before later reusing V_h in the Nitsche section
Nitsche formula uses symmetric-gradient volume energy and partial-normal velocity flux with penalty mu/h

sources.citation: T. Dupont, J. Guzman, L. R. Scott, Obtaining higher-order Galerkin accuracy when the boundary is polygonally approximated, Journal of Numerical Mathematics 33(1), 55-86 (2025), DOI 10.1515/jnma-2023-0135
facts_used: standard strong homogeneous Dirichlet FEM on a polygonal approximation is limited to H1 order h^(3/2) already for scalar quadratics
boundary corrections based on Nitsche/Taylor ideas can recover higher order
Nitsche-style methods use the full polynomial space without boundary zero restriction

sources.citation: I. G. Gjerde and L. R. Scott, Nitsche's method for Navier-Stokes equations with slip boundary conditions, Mathematics of Computation 91(334), 597-622 (2022), DOI 10.1090/mcom/3682
facts_used: Nitsche weak enforcement avoids a curved-boundary slip paradox
normal/tangent geometry approximation controls attainable convergence
projected true normals/tangents improve over raw polygon normals/tangents
current repository root contains README.md, flow_computation.py, flow_postprocess.py, solvers.py, utils.py
current solvers.py exposes strong-Dirichlet Stokes/Navier-Stokes solvers but no Scott-Vogelius-Nitsche implementation
therefore the published Nitsche tables are not reproducible from the current cited repository alone

sources.citation: R. Durst and M. Neilan, General degree divergence-free finite element methods for the Stokes problem on smooth domains, arXiv:2404.14226 (2024)
